titulo: The paper, the orange box and the name
subtitulo: What starts the clock, and what the ferry desk is legally obliged to ask
introPt: One window in Piraeus, one platform, and a paper that is not yet a ticket. Listen for the two numbers that matter.
cenario: Piraeus. A traveller buys a crossing at the ferry desk, then goes back to the metro platform with a paper ticket still unstamped.

dialogo.es: Δύο εισιτήρια για τη Νάξο, παρακαλώ.
dialogo.tts: Δύο εισιτήρια για τη Νάξο, παρακαλώ.

dialogo.es: Τα ονόματά σας και την ημερομηνία γέννησης, παρακαλώ. Αποβάθρα τέσσερα, στις οκτώ.
dialogo.pt: Your names and date of birth, please. Quay four, at eight.
dialogo.tts: Τα ονόματά σας και την ημερομηνία γέννησης, παρακαλώ. Αποβάθρα τέσσερα, στις οκτώ.

dialogo.es: Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ. Πού είναι το ακυρωτικό;
dialogo.pt: Slower, please. Where is the validating machine?
dialogo.tts: Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ. Πού είναι το ακυρωτικό;

dialogo.es: Εκεί, στην είσοδο. Ακυρώστε το πριν μπείτε.
dialogo.pt: There, at the entrance. Validate it before you get on.
dialogo.tts: Εκεί, στην είσοδο. Ακυρώστε το πριν μπείτε.

perguntas.pergunta: Why did the ferry clerk ask for names and a date of birth for a short crossing?
opcoes: Because foreign passengers are registered separately
Because the law requires the carrier to register name, sex, nationality and date of birth for every passenger
Because the fare depends on age
Because the traveller asked for two tickets rather than one
perguntas.explica: The Greek ferry ticket is a named ticket by law. Everyone in that queue is asked the same thing in the same order, and it is the carrier meeting an obligation.

perguntas.pergunta: A friend still at the hotel asks you to pick up their ferry ticket while you are at the desk. What is the problem?
opcoes: Nothing, as long as you pay in cash
The ticket carries the traveller's own name, so it cannot be bought for someone else or passed along
Only the first ticket of the day can be bought for another person
Nothing, as long as you have their phone number
perguntas.explica: The named-ticket rule is the whole point: the person sailing is the person registered. A spare ticket is not transferable to a friend.

perguntas.pergunta: The traveller bought the metro ticket forty minutes ago and has not stamped it. When do the ninety minutes start?
opcoes: At the moment of purchase, so fifty minutes are left
At midnight of the day of purchase
At the first validation, so the ninety minutes have not started at all
When the train leaves the platform
perguntas.explica: The operator states that validity counts from the ticket's first validation. Until the paper goes into the machine, the clock has not begun — which is also why buying several in advance costs you nothing.

perguntas.pergunta: What does the second half of Εκεί, στην είσοδο. Ακυρώστε το πριν μπείτε tell you to do?
opcoes: Show the ticket to the driver once you are seated
Keep the ticket until the end of the journey and hand it in
Stamp it on the way in, before boarding
Buy a second one at the entrance
perguntas.explica: Ακυρώστε is the instruction on the orange box itself, and πριν μπείτε is before you get on. The instruction is in the second half of the sentence — staying one beat past the first half is what gets you the useful part.

perguntas.pergunta: An inspector finds an unvalidated ticket. What is the honest thing to say about the amount?
opcoes: It is a fixed statutory figure printed on every ticket
It is around a hundred euros in convergent press reports, with the legal basis currently under revision
There is no penalty if you can show the receipt for the purchase
It is set by the individual inspector
perguntas.explica: The figures reported are around one hundred euros, with a reduced amount for prompt payment, and they could not be confirmed against the official gazette. Treat it as an order of magnitude — and stamp the ticket.
